note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Every count, address, schedule, price and lighting answer below comes from the City of Tallahassee's own pickleball page, which lists each outdoor venue with an address, a count line in the City's words and a weekly grid of Open Play, Reserved Play and First-Come First-Play, then defines the three terms and prices the middle one. Three community-centre pages - Walker-Ford, Jack L. McLean Jr. and Sue Herndon McCollum - supply building hours and a second copy of an address. Where the City is silent - on surface everywhere, on lighting at six of the seven venues, on parking anywhere - this page says so instead of guessing.

slots.parking: The City of Tallahassee publishes nothing about parking at any of the seven venues on this page. The word does not appear on the pickleball page, which gives each outdoor venue an address, a count line and a weekly schedule and says nothing about how to arrive, and the three community-centre pages read for this city give a street address, a phone number and opening hours without mentioning a lot. This site does not fill that gap from a map. What the City does publish shapes the trip in other ways. Four of the seven venues are community centres with courts outside the building, and the centre pages state when the building is open: Walker-Ford and McLean Monday to Saturday 9:00am to 9:00pm, and the Sue McCollum centre, which stands in Lafayette Park, Monday to Friday 9:00am to 9:00pm and Saturday from 1:00pm. That matters at Lafayette Park in particular, because the City says paddles and balls are "available inside the Sue McCollum Community Center only during regular office hours", so the equipment runs on a different clock from the courts. The McLean page lists "two comfort stations" among the park's facilities, the one mention of restrooms at any published venue; the City says nothing about restrooms elsewhere. Every published venue has a phone number on one City page or another - the centres' own numbers, and the reservation line, 850-891-4940, for Tom Brown Park and Winthrop Park.
slots.peak_hours: Tallahassee publishes a weekly timetable for its outdoor courts, and the timetable is the peak-hours answer. The rule is stated once: "All Outdoor Courts are First-Come First-Play except during the times noted below", and the times noted are Open Play, which is free and drop-in, and Reserved Play, which is booked and paid for. Open Play is where a rotation is certain to exist. At LeVerne Payne it runs Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday mornings 8:00am-12:00pm for beginners and advanced beginners, with an intermediate session on Saturday afternoons 2:00pm-5:00pm. At Tom Brown Park it runs Monday and Wednesday 8:00am-12:00pm and Sunday 8:00am-12:00pm and 5:00pm-8:30pm, with Reserved Play filling Monday to Thursday evenings 5:30pm-8:30pm and Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday mornings. Winthrop Park has no Open Play at all - Reserved Play Monday to Thursday evenings and Saturday morning, first come the rest of the week - and the City adds two claims on its courts that are not on the grid: "the GA/FL A and B league will be utilizing 5 courts on Tuesdays and 6 courts on Thursdays from 9:00am-12:00pm (September through April)" and "local school teams will be using the courts from 3:30-5:00pm (January through April)". McLean, Lafayette Park and Walker-Ford are "No Open or Reserved Play - FCFP Only", and Jake Gaither carries the one clock-time hours line in the city, "Outdoor FCFP: 8:00am - 9:00pm Daily, Closed on Sunday". Inside Open Play the City also says how the queue works: the "RACK" sets the order, games go to 11 and win by 2, and "If 6 players are waiting, players will play 9 points instead of 11 points" with all four stepping off. Outside any session, first-come play carries a 90-minute limit when others are waiting. Lighting is stated at Walker-Ford alone, "night play is available".
slots.surface_condition: The City names no surface for any pickleball court in Tallahassee. The nearest it comes is a rule at Winthrop Park, whose courts are for "tennis, pickleball and any other sports that will not damage the surface or nets of the courts" - which tells you the surface can be damaged and nothing about what it is made of. What the City does describe, venue by venue, is the hardware. LeVerne Payne has "2 courts with adjustable net straps, 4 courts with portable nets if needed and all have painted lines"; McLean has "2 courts with adjustable net straps and painted lines"; Lafayette Park has "2 courts with net tie-downs". Tom Brown is "4 pickleball courts | 8 pickleball courts on multi-purpose courts (tennis courts 1-4)", and Winthrop's six are "multi-purpose courts" in the City's word, so fourteen of the city's thirty-three outdoor courts are tennis courts taking pickleball. The one venue the City calls pickleball-only, Four Oaks Park, is not published. The one statement about condition is a closure. McLean's line reads "Due to scheduled resurfacing, both the outdoor tennis and pickleball courts at jack mclean will be unavailable for  use until december 5, 2025." - a date nine months gone when the page was read on 7 September 2026, and still there. It is printed on the venue page as the City prints it, and the build fails on the day the City removes it. Indoors, Lincoln Neighborhood Center reads "No Pickleball (renovations in progress)" on every day, and states no count.
slots.local_scene: Thirty-four verified courts across seven City venues, thirty-three of them outdoors and one inside Jake Gaither Community Center. Tom Brown Park's twelve is the largest published set; LeVerne Payne and Winthrop hold six each; Walker-Ford and Jake Gaither three; McLean and Lafayette Park two. Tallahassee is the third Florida city on this site after Cape Coral and Tampa, the first in Leon County, and the city that puts Florida over the three-city threshold for a state page. What sets it apart is how much the City writes about how play is organised. It is the first operator on this site to publish a written open-play rotation rule - the "RACK", games to 11, or to 9 once six players are waiting - and a per-session reservation price table with a senior rate: Singles $5.75, Singles Senior $4.75, Doubles $4.25, Doubles Senior $3.50, the senior rate from age 62. Two venues publish as free, LeVerne Payne and Tom Brown, because the City schedules Open Play there and writes that "all Open Play sessions are drop-in and free". The other five are unpriced first-come courts, and an unpriced court is not called free here. Five venues the City lists are not published, and they are named rather than dropped. Four Oaks Park has six courts "used for pickleball only", an Open Play and Reserved Play schedule seven days a week running to 10:00pm, online booking, and an address, "5151 Four Oaks Boulevard", that neither the Census address file nor OpenStreetMap can find - the most expensive refusal in the city. Four community centres are on the City's indoor schedule with sessions and no court count: Lawrence-Gregory Community Center at Dade Street, Lincoln Neighborhood Center, Sue Herndon McCollum Community Center, whose outdoor courts are Lafayette Park's and do publish, and the Tallahassee Senior Center, where "$3 Donation Encouraged" is printed beside the phone number. The City states no surface anywhere, lighting at one venue, and hours at one.

best_for.heading: Best if you want the most courts and a free morning
best_for.text: Tom Brown Park has twelve outdoor courts on the City's line - four standalone and eight lined onto tennis courts 1 to 4 - the largest published set in Tallahassee. Open Play, drop-in and free, runs Monday and Wednesday mornings and Sunday morning and evening; Reserved Play at $3.50 to $5.75 a session fills the weekday evenings and can be booked online. Lighting and surface are not stated.

best_for.heading: Best if you are new and want a session made for you
best_for.text: LeVerne Payne Community Center schedules "Beginner & Adv. Beginner Open Play" on Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday mornings 8:00am-12:00pm and "Intermed. Open Play" on Saturday afternoons, all free, on six courts - two with fixed nets and four painted for portable ones. The City's Wednesday-morning clinics run here too. Phone 850-891-3930. Lighting and surface are not stated.

best_for.heading: Best if you want to play after dark
best_for.text: Walker-Ford Community Center is the one Tallahassee venue where the City says its courts can be used at night: "3 courts - night play is available". The word is "night play", not "lighted", and it is published as a lighting answer on that phrase. The courts are first come, first play at all hours, with a 90-minute limit when others are waiting, and no price is stated.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does Tallahassee have?
faqs.a: We have verified 34 across seven City venues: 33 outdoor and one indoor. Tom Brown Park has twelve, LeVerne Payne and Winthrop six each, Walker-Ford and Jake Gaither three each, and McLean and Lafayette Park two each. The City also lists Four Oaks Park with six pickleball-only courts and four indoor centres with sessions but no count, none of which we can publish.

faqs.q: Is it free to play in Tallahassee?
faqs.a: During Open Play, yes, and the City says so: "all Open Play sessions are drop-in and free". Open Play is scheduled at LeVerne Payne and Tom Brown, which are the two venues published as free. Reserved Play costs $5.75 singles, $4.25 doubles, with senior rates of $4.75 and $3.50 from age 62. First-come play at the other five venues carries no stated price, so no fee answer is published for them.

The City states one: Walker-Ford Community Center, "3 courts - night play is available". That phrase, not the word lighted, is the basis of the answer. No other published venue carries a lighting statement, so the rest are recorded as unverified rather than lit or unlit. Four Oaks Park's schedule runs to 10:00pm, but a closing time is not a statement about lights, and Four Oaks is not published.

faqs.q: Why is Four Oaks Park not listed, when it has six courts?
faqs.a: Because neither address resolver can find "5151 Four Oaks Boulevard": the US Census address file returns no match and OpenStreetMap returns nothing at house-number level. Four Oaks is the City's flagship - six courts "used for pickleball only", Open Play and Reserved Play seven days a week to 10:00pm, online booking - and it fails on its address alone. It is the most expensive refusal in the city.

faqs.q: How do I reserve a court?
faqs.a: Only Reserved Play sessions can be booked; Open Play is drop-in and first-come play is not booked at all. The City takes online reservations through Court Reserve for Four Oaks Park, Tom Brown Park and Winthrop Park, or by phone on 850-891-4940 "between 9:00am and 10:00pm on weekdays / 6:00pm on weekends". For other venues with Reserved Play sessions, such as Jake Gaither's indoor court, the City says to contact the facility directly.
